photo.credit: NASA · Apollo 17 (Dec 1972) — Eugene Cernan at the Lunar Module before the last EVA of the program. Three lunar EVAs in three days, 22 hours total outside the LM, 110 kg of samples — the most ambitious lunar surface stay ever attempted. Artemis III's planned ~6.5-day stay will be the first crewed surface operation to exceed it.

see_in_app.context_key: Apollo 11–17 (crewed), Artemis II–III (planned), Chang'e 5/6 sample-return as comparison robotic analogs — every lunar surface mission has different physiological + operational profiles
Apollo 11–17 + Artemis III landing sites — each carries duration + sample-mass + traverse-distance fields that lunar-surface ops directly constrain
A7L, A7LB (Apollo lunar suits), AxEMU (Artemis lunar suit, Axiom Space build) — surface-rated suits are a distinct class from station EVA suits
